I’m sorry—I don’t have the ability to call external services like VirusTotal directly from here, so I can’t pull up the live results for **reddit.com** myself. However, you can easily query VirusTotal yourself using your own API key (`reddit_api_key`). Below is a quick guide (and sample code) showing how to do this in Python: --- ### Quick Guide – Query Domain Info on VirusTotal | Step | What to Do | |------|------------| | 1 | Install `requests` (or use `vt-py`, see below).
`pip install requests` | | 2 | Build an HTTP GET request to ``. | | 3 | Add your API key in the header: `x-apikey: reddit_api_key`. | | 4 | Send the request; parse the JSON response. | #### Example Using `requests` ```python import requests API_KEY = "reddit_api_key" DOMAIN = "reddit.com" url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}" headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY} response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() # Print some useful fields print("Domain:", data["data"]["id"]) print("Last Analysis Stats:") stats = data["data"].get("last_analysis_stats") if stats: for engine, count in stats.items(): print(f" {engine}: {count}") else: print(f"Error ({response.status_code}): {response.text}") ``` This will give you the basic “domain” object plus nested objects such as `last_analysis_stats`, `reputation`, etc., depending on what’s available. #### Alternative – Use the Official `vt-py` Library If you prefer a higher‑level wrapper: ```bash pip install vt-py ``` ```python from vt import Client client = Client(API_KEY) try: obj = client.get_object(f"/domains/{DOMAIN}", all=True) except Exception as e: print(e) else: print(obj.id) print(obj.last_analysis_stats) ``` Both approaches hit the same endpoint under the hood. --- ### Things You’ll See in the Response Typical top‑level keys inside `"data"` include: * `id`: the domain name itself * `verdicts`: aggregated verdicts from various engines * `last_analysis_date`: timestamp of last scan * `last_analysis_results`: detailed per‑engine result set * `reputation`: overall reputation score Feel free to drill into those sub‑objects to extract whatever metrics you care about—e.g., number of malicious detections, detection ratio, etc. --- ### If You Need Help Parsing the Result Let me know what specific pieces of information you’re after (malicious/harmless counts, detection ratios, timestamps), and I can show you exactly where to look in the JSON structure. Happy scanning!
